open_points.subject: model_fields.model_items model membership
open_points.text: A model is a value of one of the models of `models`, whichever it is; every other value is answered as no model.
open_points.question: Does an instance of a subclass of a specification model count as that model, and if so are only the specification model's fields returned or also fields declared by the subclass?
options: Only instances whose concrete type is exactly a model declared by `models` count; subclasses are answered as no model.
Instances of subclasses count, but only the fields declared by the specification model are returned.
Instances of subclasses count and their additional declared fields are returned.
open_points.default_guess: Require the exact concrete types declared by `models` and answer subclasses as no model.

witness.initial: A generated `Project` model exists, and another module constructs an instance of a subclass of that generated class.
events: The module calls `model_fields.model_items` with the subclass instance.
outcomes: The value is recognised as a model and its field pairs are returned.
The value is answered as no model.
witness.observer: The calling module, and ultimately any classing, binding, rendering or wire-format walk using the result.

open_points.subject: model_fields.model_items contract representation
open_points.text: For a model, its declared fields as name and value pairs in their declared order, a nested model given as a value and not opened; for any other value, that it is no model.
open_points.question: What exact State 6 result form distinguishes an empty model from a non-model and carries the ordered name/value pairs?
options: Return `None` for a non-model and an ordered sequence of pairs for a model, including an empty sequence for a model with no fields.
Return a discriminated result model with separate `model` and `not_model` variants.
Return a pair consisting of an `is_model` flag and an ordered sequence of field pairs.
consequences: The nullable form is compact but requires the contract to distinguish `None` from an empty sequence precisely.
A discriminated result is explicit but adds a contract model and corresponding model/import surface.
A flag-and-items pair avoids a new result model but permits meaningless combinations unless State 6 constrains them.
open_points.requirement: For a model, its declared fields as name and value pairs in their declared order, a nested model given as a value and not opened; for any other value, that it is no model.

open_points.subject: model_fields model recognition and field discovery
open_points.text: How a model's declared fields and their order are found.
open_points.question: What State 7 mechanism recognises exactly the specification's generated model values and obtains their specification-declared field order without naming individual models?
options: Inspect generated class metadata and verify that the concrete class belongs to the generated `models` module.
Use a shared nominal base or marker implemented by the model emitter and recognised by `model_fields`.
Use a generated field-access protocol plus a nominal provenance marker so unrelated structurally similar objects are rejected.
consequences: Class/module metadata needs no individual model imports but must define exact-type, subclass and spoofing behaviour.
A shared base or marker gives a direct nominal test but requires emitter cooperation and an accurately declared dependency/import surface.
A protocol supports generated variants uniformly, but a structural protocol alone would violate the promise that every other value is answered as no model, so it also needs nominal provenance.
open_points.requirement: A model is a value of one of the models of `models`, whichever it is; every other value is answered as no model. Nothing. It reads values of the models of `models` without naming any of them.
